newsitem.title: USA: CHESS-Kasparov, Deep Blue draw fifth game.
newsitem.headline: CHESS-Kasparov, Deep Blue draw fifth game.

text.p: World chess champion Garry Kasparov and the IBM supercomputer Deep Blue drew for the third consecutive time on Saturday in the fifth game of their $1.1 million re-match.

The computer program stunned the Russian grandmaster by forcing the draw with what expert observers considered to be unconventional moves in a tense endgame. The match is tied at 2-1/2 points each after one win each and three draws. The sixth and final game is scheduled for Sunday.
Kasparov, in a re-match with the chess-playing program he defeated in Philadelphia in 1996, agreed to the draw with the Deep Blue programmers after 49 moves and more than four hours play.

The champion achieved an advantage out of the opening, a King's Indian Attack, but appeared to lose the edge until Deep Blue permitted an exchange of queens that critically disrupted its pawn structure.
Kasparov faltered in the endgame as the program maneuvered its black pieces artfully into a drawn game.

"He blew the win against the tenacity of the machine," said international master and commentator Maurice Ashley as Kasparov remained at the board for several minutes, gesturing with his hands and talking to his advisers and match arbiters.
